MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
May 22, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A special meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 6:00 p.m., on Wednesday,
May 22, 2013, in the Assembly Room, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Sanchez led the salute to the flag.

c.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Recreation
Supervisor Vida, Associate Engineer Shabazi and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

None.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

None.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

5.  BUDGET WORKSHOP - PROPOSED FY 2013/14 BUDGET
  A. Budget Overview – City Manager Rock
  B. General Administration – City Manager Rock
  C. Administrative Services Department - Administrative Services Director Chavez
  D. Community Development Department – Assistant City Manager Sugano
  E. Community Services Department - Community Services Director McPherron
  F. Parks and Recreation Department - Parks and Recreation Director Harding

  Page 1
   G. Public Works Department - Public Works Director Damasse
Discussion and possible direction to staff regarding proposed budget for FY 2013/14.

City Manager Rock provided an overview of the proposed budget and outlined the major
changes in the budget for FY 2013/14; City Manager Rock also noted that the format of the
budget had been changed in order to make it more user-friendly. According to City Manager
Rock, the total proposed budget is $14,650,804, which includes the General Fund budget of
$7,721,747. City Manager Rock stated that the budget is balanced, without the use of the
General Fund Reserve, however, carry-over funds and two one-time revenue sources from FY
2012/13 were used to balance the budget. Some of the major changes, mentioned by City
Manager Rock, to the proposed budget include: the transfer of salary and benefit costs from the
Water Fund to the General Fund, in the amount of $171,054, which was based on the Water
Fund Salary Allocation Study; an increase in the LA County Sheriff’s contract of 2.4%, or
$62,597; the elimination of two full-time positions (Human Resources Officer and Community
Services Specialist), which resulted in General Fund cost savings of $194,801; the creation of a
special fund for the Stephenson Center Improvement Project, in the amount of $50,000; and the
funding of the emergency generator project, in the amount of $83,000. Another major change
specifically outlined by City Manager Rock was the creation of a Restricted Fund in the amount
of $60,000, as the City needs to begin reducing its reliance on the $300,000 in annual royalty
fees received from Chandler Sand and Gravel, especially since there is the possibility of
Chandler closing operations sometime in the near future. City Manager Rock also pointed out
that overhead costs for the Water Fund had been reinstated in proposed budget, in the amount
of $112,000, to which Councilmember Traina asked for a detailed breakdown of those costs.

City Manager Rock stated that the City is doing okay financially, although since the City is not
wealthy, it needs to start long-term planning to take into account rising health care costs, PERS
costs, and overall operational costs.

City Manager Rock provided an overview of the General Administration budget, which includes
City Council, the City Attorney, and the City Manager / City Clerk budgets (Attachment 1).
According to City Manager Rock, the total budget request for General Administration is
$828,397. City Manager Rock mentioned that staff had been reduced from five full-time
employees to 4 full-time employees, as the Administrative Secretary position was eliminated.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question as to why there was no money budgeted for
groundwater leasing, City Manager Rock responded that the City went out twice for bids, but no
bids were received. Councilmember Traina suggested explaining this in the budget summary
portion of the budget.

Councilmember Sanchez recommended increasing the travel and training per Councilmember,
from $2,000 to $3,000, as networking is an important aspect of a Councilmembers’ job.
Councilmembers Gazeley and Savidan agreed with Councilmember Sanchez. Councilmember
Sanchez moved to increase Councilmembers’ travel and training expenses to $3,000.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:

AYES: Councilmembers Sanchez, Savidan, and Gazeley

NOES: Councilmember Traina and Mayor Estrada
  Page 2
 Discussion followed on what the procedure would be if one Councilmember spends more than
their budgeted $3,000 for travel and training. Mayor Estrada stated that Councilmembers would
need approval to spend over their $3,000 allocation, as additional expenditures would be taken
from other Councilmembers, and it should be agreed upon ahead of time.

City Manager Rock stated that the City Attorney is paid an $8,000 per month flat rate, and that
costs for litigation and code enforcements are paid separately. According to City Manager
Rock, the City Attorney’s cost had been reduced to $160,000.

Mayor Estrada noted that the moving expenses budgeted under the City Manager’s budget
would be discussed separately during the City Manager’s evaluation.

Councilmember Traina pointed out that overtime costs are still high and recommended reducing
such costs. Councilmember Traina also stated that cell phone charges were high, and
suggested that those costs could be reduced as well.

Discussion followed on whether contributions to outside agencies were justifiable, as the other
jurisdictions are currently cutting those costs, and the City has already had to reduce its costs by
laying-off employees. In response to the question of whether contributions were allowed to
outside organizations, including City affiliated organizations such as Sister City, City Attorney
Hogin stated that contributions to other organizations are allowable, as long as they provide a
direct benefit for the taxpayers.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the $1,000 contribution to the Lomita Little League,
and the $1,000 contribution for Sister City. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion.
Councilmember Traina expressed his concern with giving money to outside organizations, and
Mayor Estrada agreed with him. Councilmember Sanchez pulled his second on the motion.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to budget $2,000 in the outside organization contribution line
item without specifically identifying at this time which organization would receive funding, as that
could be determined at a later date. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.
Councilmember Traina made a substitute motion to eliminate all contributions to outside
agencies. Mayor Estrada seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:

AYES: Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada

NOES: Councilmembers Gazeley and Savidan

Mayor Estrada stated that the proposed increase in the City Manager’s contract would be
determined during the City Manager’s performance evaluation, which is currently scheduled for
June 3, 2013.

Administrative Services Director Chavez provided an overview of the different functions
provided by the Administrative Services Department. In response to Councilmember Gazeley’s

  Page 3
 question regarding the General Fund Reserve, Director Chavez responded that there is
currently $3.8 million in the General Fund Reserve.

Assistant City Manager / Community Development Director Sugano provided an overview of the
various divisions of the Community Development Department, as well as major budget changes
for the Department. Councilmember Traina stated that he was concerned that 12% of the total
costs for the Community Development Department were budgeted under the Water Fund, which
Councilmember Traina stated seems high. Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that the
Water Fund Salary Allocation Study had corrected those allocation issues, and that the
percentage included some services like Information Technology, and staff assistance with water
quality complaints.

Community Services Director McPherron provided an overview of the services provided by the
Community Services Department, as well as the Department’s budget requests.

City Manager Rock stated that it is becoming more and more costly each year to operate Lomita
Manor, and that the City does not know how much annual funding will be allocated by Housing
and Urban Development (HUD) and CDBG; if the full amount is not received, City Manager
Rock stated that subsidies from the General Fund would be required to cover operational costs.

In response to Councilmember Savidan’s question as to why the City contracted out the
processing of parking citations to the City of Inglewood, and why such processing could not be
done in-house, Director McPherron stated that the City would need to purchase software and
hire another staff person if the processing were to be done in-house.

Councilmember Traina requested that the Sheriff’s Department provide a breakdown of the
patrol services provided to the Cypress Water Production Facility. City Manager Rock stated
that the patrol costs were estimated and were adequate for a $12 million facility; the patrol costs
were budgeted at $25,000 for the entire year. Councilmember Traina disagreed.

Mayor Estrada asked that the costs on Page 68, Line Item 5755, regarding mobile command
center be adjusted, as the total amount should be $30,000, not $23,670; no expenses had been
incurred to date. Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that staff would verify this line item.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question on whether health care reform would affect the
City, City Manager Rock responded that the City would not need to provide health benefits to
part-time employees, as the new law only applies to organizations that have over 50 full-time
employees.

Assistant City Manager Sugano provided an overview of the budget for the Parks and
Recreation Department budget. In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding why
the travel and training costs had increased under the Parks and Recreation Department, City
Manager Rock stated that in the past this line item had been completely eliminated, but was
reinstated this year in order to allow staff to attend conferences.

Mayor Estrada recommended eliminating the funding for Movies Under the Stars, which in turn
would save the City $6,000. Discussion followed that the event was the only entertainment

  Page 4
 provided by the City for the residents. Mayor Estrada moved to eliminate the funding for Movies
Under the Stars from the budget. Discussion followed regarding the actual cost of the event,
including salaries, which was stated totaled roughly $7,000. The motion failed for the lack of
second.

Councilmember Traina was concerned that maintenance workers receive a lot of overtime pay,
to which City Manager Rock stated they will continue to be diligent about monitoring this
expense. Councilmember Savidan agreed that overtime costs should be limited. Mayor
Estrada recommended flexing employees’ schedules in order to eliminate overtime.

Public Works Director Damasse provided an overview of the Public Works Department budget,
and stated that out of the total $4.5 million, $2.1 million had been budgeted for the purchase of
Metropolitan Water.

Councilmember Traina inquired about the certifications of staff at the Cypress Water Production
Facility (CWPF), to which City Manager Rock responded that Water Works is still running the
CWPF at this time, and that the newly hired Water Treatment Operator has T-4 and D-3
certifications, which is more than what is required to operate the CWPF. Director Damasse also
provided information regarding the certification of the other Public Works staff. In response to
Councilmember Traina’s question regarding the term of the contract with Water Works, and
when that contract would end, City Manager Rock stated that once the new Water Treatment
Operator has been fully trained, then the contract with Water Works will be reduced; City
Manager Rock estimated the contract term to be less than a year.

In response to the question regarding the budgeted cost, of $45,000, for the Water Rate Study,
Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that staff will be looking at the operational costs
associated with the CWPF, and at some point a revised Water Rate Study would need to be
conducted.

Councilmember Traina asked whether the cost of purchasing Metropolitan Water could be
reduced, since the City is now using well water, to which Assistant City Manager Sugano
responded that based on only two months of operation data, it is currently difficult to calculate
the actual amount needed to cover the cost of purchasing Metropolitan Water; furthermore, the
MWD water cost to the City had increased, which has not been passed on to the rate payers.

City Manager Rock concluded the overall proposed budget presentation with an outline of the
major accomplishments that City Council completed, along with City Staff, during FY 2012/13,
which included: hiring a new City Manager; started distribution of blended water from Well No. 5;
approved a five year Capital Improvement Plan Budget; conducted the City’s first Annual
Strategic Planning Workshop; adopted mission, vision and core values for the City; adopted a
Records Retention Policy and Schedule; reorganized the City’s customer service functions;
reviewed all operating expenses related to materials, supplies, and vendor contracts, which
resulted in a savings of $10,000; and eliminated three full-time positions.

  Page 5
 ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8.53 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
